# Annual Leave Policy

Document family: `family.hr.annual-leave`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Full-time employees receive 28 days of paid annual leave including public holidays. Requests for five or more consecutive working days must be submitted at least four weeks in advance.

Managers should respond within ten working days. No more than five unused days may be carried into the next leave year with written approval.

# Outbreak Visiting Restrictions Procedure

Document family: `family.visitors.outbreak-restrictions`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 October 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

During a declared outbreak, routine indoor visiting is paused for all residents. Essential end-of-life visits require manager approval and visitors must follow the PPE instructions given on arrival.

The manager reviews restrictions every seven days with infection-control advice.

# Sickness Absence Procedure

Document family: `family.hr.sickness-absence`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Employees must telephone their line manager personally at least one hour before the shift begins. A text message is not sufficient unless an emergency prevents a call.

A return-to-work conversation is completed after every absence. A fit note is required from the eighth calendar day of continuous absence.

# Data Protection Policy

Document family: `family.gdpr.data-protection`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2024
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Personal information must be collected for a defined purpose, limited to what is necessary, kept accurate and retained only as long as required. Staff must lock paper records away and use approved systems for electronic records.

Suspected disclosure to the wrong person must be reported to the Data Protection Officer within twenty-four hours.

# Moving and Handling Policy

Document family: `family.health-safety.moving-handling`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 October 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Staff follow the person's moving-and-handling plan and use the named equipment. Two staff are required for every full-body hoist transfer. Any equipment defect is reported and the equipment removed from use.

The plan is reviewed annually or after a fall, material mobility change or equipment change.

# Complaints Handling Policy

Document family: `family.complaints.handling`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 July 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Staff acknowledge a complaint within three working days. The investigating manager aims to issue the written outcome within twenty working days and explains any unavoidable delay.

A complaint may be verbal or written. Staff must not require the complainant to complete a form before concerns are recorded.

# Medication Competency Assessment

Document family: `family.training.medication-competency`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2024
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Assessment element | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| MAR reading | Correctly identifies medicine, dose and time |
| Administration | Three directly observed medication rounds |
| PRN | Explains indication and records outcome |

Competency is reassessed every twelve months and after a significant medication error.

# Fire Drill and Debrief Procedure

Document family: `family.fire.drills`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Each service completes a fire drill at least every six months. Drills should rotate across shifts so night staff participate at least annually. The record includes alarm time, evacuation duration, staff present, simulated conditions and actions agreed.

The registered manager reviews the drill within five working days and assigns actions with owners and dates.

# Safe Administration of Medicines Policy

Document family: `family.medication.administration`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2024
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

## Purpose

This policy describes the minimum controls for staff who administer medicines
to people supported by Alderbridge Care Group. Only staff whose training and
competency assessment are current may administer medicines without direct
supervision.

## Administration record

The member of staff administering a medicine must sign the Medication
Administration Record (MAR) immediately after the person has taken the dose.
The signature must never be added before administration. Where a dose is not
given, staff must enter the correct MAR exception code and add a concise note.

## Checks before administration

Before giving a medicine, staff must confirm the person's identity, medicine, dose, route and scheduled time against the MAR.
Staff must also check the label
is legible and the medicine is within its expiry date. For medicines stored in
a refrigerator, the most recent recorded temperature must be within the
approved range before the medicine is removed for administration.

## Missed or refused doses

A refused dose must be recorded using code R.
Staff should explain the purpose of the medicine without coercion and notify the
shift leader when the care plan requires escalation. A dose that is unavailable
must be recorded using code U.

## PRN medicines

Before administering a PRN medicine, staff must consult the person's current
PRN protocol. The reason, dose and observed outcome must be recorded.

## Audit

The registered manager arranges a monthly MAR audit. Any unexplained gap is
treated as a medication incident and reviewed under the medication error
procedure.

# Allegations Against Staff Procedure

Document family: `family.safeguarding.allegations-staff`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 October 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

The registered manager protects the person supported, preserves evidence and informs the safeguarding lead. The employee who is the subject of an allegation must not be asked to investigate or contact witnesses. Suspension is considered only after an initial risk assessment and is not an automatic finding of fault.

The manager informs HR within one working day and coordinates external notifications with safeguarding and police where required.

# Accident and Incident Reporting Procedure

Document family: `family.health-safety.accident-reporting`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 July 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Staff first make the area safe, provide first aid and obtain emergency assistance. Every accident, near miss or dangerous occurrence is recorded before the end of the shift. The manager reviews whether the event may be reportable under RIDDOR and contacts the health and safety lead within two working days.

# Controlled Drugs Procedure

Document family: `family.medication.controlled-drugs`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 June 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Two authorised members of staff must witness every controlled-drug administration and sign the controlled-drugs register immediately. The running balance is checked after each entry. A discrepancy is reported to the registered manager before the end of the shift and the stock is secured while the check is repeated.

Expired stock remains in the controlled-drugs cabinet, clearly segregated, until collected by the supplying pharmacy. Staff must not destroy controlled drugs without an authorised witness and the required record.

# Hand Hygiene Procedure

Document family: `family.infection.hand-hygiene`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Use liquid soap and water when hands are visibly dirty and after caring for a person with vomiting or diarrhoea. Alcohol hand rub may be used for routine decontamination when hands are visibly clean. Staff wash for at least 20 seconds and dry with a disposable towel.

Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Each service completes a fire drill at least every six months. Drills should rotate across shifts so night staff participate at least annually. The record includes alarm time, evacuation duration, staff present, simulated conditions and actions agreed.

The registered manager reviews the drill within five working days and assigns actions with owners and dates.

# Safe Administration of Medicines Policy

Document family: `family.medication.administration`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2024
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

## Purpose

This policy describes the minimum controls for staff who administer medicines
to people supported by Alderbridge Care Group. Only staff whose training and
competency assessment are current may administer medicines without direct
supervision.

## Administration record

The member of staff administering a medicine must sign the Medication
Administration Record (MAR) immediately after the person has taken the dose.
The signature must never be added before administration. Where a dose is not
given, staff must enter the correct MAR exception code and add a concise note.

## Checks before administration

Before giving a medicine, staff must confirm the person's identity, medicine, dose, route and scheduled time against the MAR.
Staff must also check the label
is legible and the medicine is within its expiry date. For medicines stored in
a refrigerator, the most recent recorded temperature must be within the
approved range before the medicine is removed for administration.

## Missed or refused doses

A refused dose must be recorded using code R.
Staff should explain the purpose of the medicine without coercion and notify the
shift leader when the care plan requires escalation. A dose that is unavailable
must be recorded using code U.

## PRN medicines

Before administering a PRN medicine, staff must consult the person's current
PRN protocol. The reason, dose and observed outcome must be recorded.

## Audit

The registered manager arranges a monthly MAR audit. Any unexplained gap is
treated as a medication incident and reviewed under the medication error
procedure.

# Allegations Against Staff Procedure

Document family: `family.safeguarding.allegations-staff`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 October 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

The registered manager protects the person supported, preserves evidence and informs the safeguarding lead. The employee who is the subject of an allegation must not be asked to investigate or contact witnesses. Suspension is considered only after an initial risk assessment and is not an automatic finding of fault.

The manager informs HR within one working day and coordinates external notifications with safeguarding and police where required.

Document family: `family.health-safety.accident-reporting`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 July 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Staff first make the area safe, provide first aid and obtain emergency assistance. Every accident, near miss or dangerous occurrence is recorded before the end of the shift. The manager reviews whether the event may be reportable under RIDDOR and contacts the health and safety lead within two working days.

# Controlled Drugs Procedure

Document family: `family.medication.controlled-drugs`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 June 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Two authorised members of staff must witness every controlled-drug administration and sign the controlled-drugs register immediately. The running balance is checked after each entry. A discrepancy is reported to the registered manager before the end of the shift and the stock is secured while the check is repeated.

Expired stock remains in the controlled-drugs cabinet, clearly segregated, until collected by the supplying pharmacy. Staff must not destroy controlled drugs without an authorised witness and the required record.

# Hand Hygiene Procedure

Document family: `family.infection.hand-hygiene`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Use liquid soap and water when hands are visibly dirty and after caring for a person with vomiting or diarrhoea. Alcohol hand rub may be used for routine decontamination when hands are visibly clean. Staff wash for at least 20 seconds and dry with a disposable towel.
